items.title: Persistent worry
items.text: During the past several months, I have worried excessively about multiple areas of life more days than not.

items.title: Hard to turn off
items.text: Once I start worrying or feeling afraid, it is hard for me to shut it off or calm my mind.

items.title: Restless or keyed up
items.text: I often feel keyed up, restless, on edge, or unable to fully relax.

items.title: Physical tension
items.text: Anxiety often shows up in my body through tension, tight muscles, shakiness, stomach upset, or similar symptoms.

items.title: Sudden surges
items.text: I have episodes where fear or discomfort suddenly rises quickly and feels overwhelming.

items.title: Body alarm reaction
items.text: During anxious moments, I may have a racing heart, shortness of breath, dizziness, sweating, or a feeling that something is very wrong.

items.title: Avoiding because of fear
items.text: I avoid places, situations, conversations, travel, or responsibilities because of fear, worry, or panic-like feelings.

items.title: Repeated checking or reassurance
items.text: I repeatedly seek reassurance, check things, or mentally review situations because I am afraid something bad will happen.

items.title: Sleep affected
items.text: My anxiety has noticeably disrupted my sleep or made it hard to rest deeply.

items.title: Unusually up or irritable
items.text: I have had clear periods where I felt unusually energized, intensely driven, unusually upbeat, or much more irritable than normal for me.

items.title: Needed much less sleep
items.text: During those periods, I needed much less sleep than usual and still felt energized rather than tired.

items.title: Racing thoughts
items.text: During those periods, my thoughts moved unusually fast or jumped rapidly from one thing to another.

items.title: More talkative
items.text: During those periods, I talked much more than usual, felt pressure to keep talking, or found it hard to slow down.

items.title: Unusually driven or active
items.text: During those periods, I became unusually productive, busy, restless, ambitious, or driven to start many things.

items.title: Agitated or wound up
items.text: During those periods, I felt internally revved up, physically agitated, or unable to settle.

items.title: Unusually confident
items.text: During those periods, I felt unusually powerful, confident, important, gifted, or certain in ways that were noticeably above my baseline.

items.title: Risky or impulsive behavior
items.text: During those periods, I made unusually impulsive or risky choices involving spending, sex, driving, business, substances, conflict, or major decisions.

items.title: Others noticed a change
items.text: Other people noticed that I was acting very different from my usual self during these periods.

items.title: Low mood
items.text: During the past 2 weeks, I have felt down, sad, empty, or hopeless for much of the day.

items.title: Loss of interest
items.text: During the past 2 weeks, I have lost interest or pleasure in activities I usually enjoy.

items.title: Sleep change
items.text: During the past 2 weeks, my sleep has been noticeably different than usual (trouble falling asleep, waking often, waking too early, or sleeping much more).

items.title: Appetite or weight change
items.text: During the past 2 weeks, my appetite has changed a lot (much less or much more), or my weight has noticeably changed (without trying).

items.title: Slowed down or restless
items.text: During the past 2 weeks, I have felt slowed down (moving/speaking more slowly) or unusually restless/fidgety.

items.title: Low energy
items.text: During the past 2 weeks, I have had very low energy or fatigue most of the time.

items.title: Worthlessness or guilt
items.text: During the past 2 weeks, I have felt worthless or excessively guilty (more than makes sense for the situation).

items.title: Focus or decisions
items.text: During the past 2 weeks, I have had trouble concentrating, thinking clearly, or making decisions.

items.title: Thoughts about death
items.text: During the past 2 weeks, I have had frequent thoughts about death, wishing I wouldn’t wake up, or thoughts of harming myself.

items.title: Detached from self
items.text: At times I feel detached from myself, as if I am observing myself from outside.

items.title: World feels unreal
items.text: At times the world around me feels unreal, dreamlike, foggy, or distant.

items.title: Memory gaps
items.text: I have gaps in memory for things I should likely remember.

items.title: Lost time
items.text: I sometimes lose track of time or realize more time passed than I can account for.

items.title: Identity discontinuity
items.text: At times I feel like different parts of me take over in ways that affect memory, behavior, or continuity.

items.title: Numbing or shutdown
items.text: When overwhelmed, I can go numb, blank, or mentally shut down.

items.title: Stress-triggered
items.text: These experiences tend to become stronger under stress, conflict, or trauma reminders.

items.title: Confusion afterward
items.text: After these experiences, I may feel confused, disoriented, or uncertain about what happened.

items.title: Function disruption
items.text: These experiences have disrupted work, relationships, safety, or daily responsibilities.

items.title: Restriction
items.text: I restrict food, calories, or eating in ways that feel hard to control or increasingly rigid.

items.title: Fear of weight gain
items.text: Fear of gaining weight strongly influences my eating or behavior.

items.title: Body image preoccupation
items.text: My self-worth is strongly affected by weight, shape, or body image.

items.title: Binge-like eating
items.text: I sometimes eat a large amount in a way that feels out of control.

items.title: Compensatory behavior
items.text: I use unhealthy strategies to compensate for eating, such as purging, over-exercise, or strict correction afterward.

items.title: Guilt or shame after eating
items.text: After eating, I often feel intense guilt, shame, disgust, or panic.

items.title: Food rituals
items.text: My eating has become unusually ritualized, rigid, rule-bound, or fear-driven.

items.title: Avoiding eating with others
items.text: I avoid meals, restaurants, or social eating situations because of anxiety, shame, or control concerns.

items.title: Physical consequences
items.text: This pattern has affected my energy, mood, body functioning, or health.

items.title: Urine accidents
items.text: I have repeated problems with bladder control when control would normally be expected.

items.title: Bowel accidents
items.text: I have repeated problems with bowel control when control would normally be expected.

items.title: Urgency
items.text: I feel strong urgency that is hard to control before accidents or near-accidents.

items.title: Avoidance
items.text: I avoid travel, activities, sleepovers, work, or social situations because of fear of accidents.

items.title: Embarrassment
items.text: This pattern causes strong embarrassment, shame, or secrecy.

items.title: Planning around bathrooms
items.text: My routines are heavily shaped by needing immediate access to bathrooms or extra precautions.

items.title: Sleep disruption
items.text: This pattern disrupts sleep, bedding, or overnight comfort.

items.title: Internal mismatch
items.text: I experience a significant mismatch between my internal sense of gender and my body or assigned/socially expected gender.

items.title: Body-related distress
items.text: Parts of my body or physical sex characteristics cause significant distress or discomfort.

items.title: Social-role distress
items.text: Being treated as a gender that does not fit me causes strong distress or discomfort.

items.title: Wish for different embodiment
items.text: I strongly wish aspects of my body or social gendered experience were different.

items.title: Persistent identity concern
items.text: This is not just occasional questioning; it has felt meaningful and persistent.

items.title: Avoidance
items.text: I avoid mirrors, clothing, social roles, intimacy, or settings that intensify this discomfort.

items.title: Mood impact
items.text: This pattern contributes to sadness, anxiety, shame, or emotional distress.

items.title: Anger outbursts
items.text: I have repeated anger outbursts that feel excessive for the situation.

items.title: Aggression
items.text: I become verbally or physically aggressive in ways I later regret.

items.title: Damaging things
items.text: I have damaged property, thrown things, or become physically destructive during anger or impulse states.

items.title: Rule-breaking
items.text: I knowingly break important rules, boundaries, or expectations despite consequences.

items.title: Deceit or manipulation
items.text: I use deception, concealment, or manipulation in ways that create problems.

items.title: Low frustration tolerance
items.text: I become intensely frustrated or reactive more quickly than seems typical.

items.title: Regret afterward
items.text: Afterward I often feel regret, shame, or recognize I reacted badly.

items.title: Risky impulses
items.text: I act impulsively in ways that create conflict, danger, or serious consequences.

items.title: Memory decline
items.text: My memory feels noticeably worse than it used to be.

items.title: Attention decline
items.text: I am less able to sustain attention or keep track of tasks than before.

items.title: Word-finding difficulty
items.text: I more often struggle to find words or keep language clear.

items.title: Planning/executive difficulty
items.text: Planning, judgment, sequencing, or problem-solving feels harder than before.

items.title: Disorientation
items.text: I sometimes feel more confused about time, place, or what I was doing.

items.title: Slowed thinking
items.text: My thinking feels slower or less efficient than it used to be.

items.title: Errors in daily tasks
items.text: I make more mistakes in normal daily tasks than I used to.

items.title: Drop in functioning
items.text: My independence or overall functioning has dropped because of these changes.

items.title: Distractibility
items.text: Since childhood, I have had persistent difficulty sustaining attention or staying on task.

items.title: Organization
items.text: Planning, organizing, prioritizing, and following multi-step tasks has been persistently difficult for me.

items.title: Forgetfulness
items.text: I frequently lose track of items, instructions, appointments, or responsibilities.

items.title: Restlessness
items.text: I have often felt unusually restless, fidgety, or unable to stay still when expected.

items.title: Impulsivity
items.text: I often interrupt, act before thinking, or struggle to wait my turn.

items.title: Social cues
items.text: Understanding social cues, tone, timing, or unspoken rules has often been harder for me than for peers.

items.title: Rigidity or sameness
items.text: Changes in routine, unexpected transitions, or not knowing what to expect can be unusually stressful for me.

items.title: Sensory sensitivity
items.text: Noise, textures, lights, touch, or other sensory input can feel overwhelming or unusually intense for me.

items.title: Learning differences
items.text: I have had longstanding unevenness in learning, processing speed, reading, writing, math, or communication.

items.title: Intrusive thoughts/images/urges
items.text: I have unwanted thoughts, images, doubts, or urges that enter my mind repeatedly and feel disturbing or difficult to ignore.

items.title: Hard to dismiss
items.text: When these intrusions show up, it feels hard to simply let them pass without reacting to them.

items.title: Checking
items.text: I repeatedly check things such as locks, appliances, messages, mistakes, safety, health, or whether I may have caused harm.

items.title: Cleaning or arranging
items.text: I feel driven to clean, wash, organize, or arrange things in a particular way to reduce discomfort or make things feel right.

items.title: Counting or repeating
items.text: I repeat actions, words, numbers, or routines until they feel complete, safe, or correct.

items.title: Mental rituals
items.text: I silently review, pray, cancel out thoughts, replay events, or mentally neutralize things to reduce anxiety.

items.title: Reassurance
items.text: I repeatedly ask others for reassurance, confirmation, or certainty because the doubt won’t settle.

items.title: Consumes time
items.text: These thoughts or habits take a lot of time, energy, or mental space during the day.

items.title: Anxiety if resisted
items.text: If I try not to do the routine or not respond to the thought, my anxiety or discomfort rises noticeably.

items.title: Distressing sexual interests
items.text: Some sexual thoughts, fantasies, or urges feel distressing, unwanted, or hard to reconcile with my values.

items.title: Preoccupation
items.text: These thoughts or urges take up a lot of mental space or return repeatedly.

items.title: Loss of control
items.text: I feel I may not always have full control over these urges or behaviors.

items.title: Secrecy or shame
items.text: This area is associated with significant secrecy, shame, or fear of exposure.

items.title: Relationship impact
items.text: This pattern has affected trust, intimacy, or relationship stability.

items.title: Functional impact
items.text: This pattern affects work, concentration, daily life, or emotional stability.

items.title: Boundary risk
items.text: I worry this pattern could lead to crossing boundaries, acting unsafely, or causing harm.

items.title: Relationship instability
items.text: My relationships have often been intense, unstable, conflictual, or repeatedly disrupted.

items.title: Identity instability
items.text: My sense of self, values, or direction can feel unstable or difficult to maintain.

items.title: Rigidity
items.text: I tend to be unusually rigid, controlling, inflexible, or unable to adapt compared with others.

items.title: Suspiciousness
items.text: I often feel guarded, mistrustful, or unsure of others’ motives.

items.title: Emotional instability
items.text: My emotions can shift intensely or feel difficult to regulate.

items.title: Detached or avoidant style
items.text: I often keep distance, withdraw, or avoid closeness in ways that affect relationships.

items.title: Attention or validation seeking
items.text: I may strongly seek reassurance, admiration, attention, or emotional confirmation from others.

items.title: Impulsivity
items.text: I make impulsive choices that repeatedly create problems.

items.title: Strong interpersonal reactivity
items.text: How others respond to me strongly affects my mood, self-image, or behavior.

items.title: Hearing things
items.text: I have heard voices or sounds that others around me did not seem to hear.

items.title: Seeing things
items.text: I have seen things, shadows, figures, or visual events that others around me did not seem to see.

items.title: Fixed beliefs
items.text: I have had beliefs that felt completely certain even when others strongly disagreed or said they were unlikely.

items.title: Suspiciousness
items.text: I have felt strongly that people were watching me, talking about me, or trying to harm me.

items.title: Thought confusion
items.text: My thoughts have at times felt jumbled, hard to organize, or hard to communicate clearly.

items.title: Thought influence
items.text: I have felt as if thoughts were being inserted, removed, read, or influenced in unusual ways.

items.title: Withdrawal or flatness
items.text: I have become markedly withdrawn, emotionally flat, or disconnected from normal life compared to my earlier self.

items.title: Disorganized behavior
items.text: Others may have seen me as acting very oddly, disorganized, or hard to follow.

items.title: Drop in functioning
items.text: My overall functioning has noticeably dropped during periods when these experiences were stronger.

items.title: Low desire
items.text: I have persistent difficulty with sexual desire or interest compared with what feels normal for me.

items.title: Arousal difficulty
items.text: I have persistent difficulty becoming mentally or physically aroused.

items.title: Orgasm difficulty
items.text: I have persistent difficulty reaching orgasm or climax.

items.title: Pain or discomfort
items.text: Sexual activity is affected by pain, discomfort, or strong physical difficulty.

items.title: Avoidance
items.text: I avoid sexual contact or intimacy because of these concerns.

items.title: Distress
items.text: These concerns cause me meaningful frustration, sadness, shame, or distress.

items.title: Relationship strain
items.text: These concerns have created strain, misunderstanding, or conflict in my relationship(s).

items.title: Trouble falling asleep
items.text: I often have significant trouble falling asleep.

items.title: Trouble staying asleep
items.text: I often wake during the night and struggle to return to sleep.

items.title: Waking too early
items.text: I often wake too early and cannot return to sleep.

items.title: Sleeping too much
items.text: I may sleep far more than expected and still not feel restored.

items.title: Unrefreshing sleep
items.text: Even when I sleep enough hours, the sleep often does not feel refreshing.

items.title: Daytime sleepiness
items.text: I struggle with sleepiness, fatigue, or nodding off during the day.

items.title: Anxiety about sleep
items.text: Worry about sleep itself has become part of the problem.

items.title: Safety or functioning risk
items.text: Sleep problems have affected driving, concentration, work, or safety.

items.title: Body preoccupation
items.text: Physical symptoms or body sensations become a major focus of my attention.

items.title: Health worry
items.text: I often worry that normal sensations or minor symptoms could mean something serious.

items.title: Checking
items.text: I repeatedly monitor, inspect, or check my body for signs of illness.

items.title: Searching for answers
items.text: I spend significant time researching symptoms or illnesses online.

items.title: Reassurance-seeking
items.text: I repeatedly seek reassurance from others or providers about my health.

items.title: Catastrophic interpretation
items.text: I tend to quickly assume bodily symptoms could mean something severe or dangerous.

items.title: Avoidance
items.text: I avoid activities, foods, exercise, travel, or responsibilities because I fear symptoms or illness.

items.title: Distress
items.text: Even when others are not alarmed, my symptoms cause me intense distress or fear.

items.title: Time cost
items.text: Health-related worry or checking takes a large amount of time or mental energy.

items.title: More than intended
items.text: I use more than I mean to, or for longer than I plan to.

items.title: Trouble cutting down
items.text: I have tried to cut down or stop and found it difficult.

items.title: Craving
items.text: I experience strong urges or cravings to use.

items.title: Time spent
items.text: A significant amount of time goes into getting, using, recovering, or thinking about use.

items.title: Responsibilities affected
items.text: Use has caused problems in responsibilities or normal roles.

items.title: Continued despite harm
items.text: I continue despite physical, emotional, or relationship harm.

items.title: Tolerance
items.text: I need more than before to get the same effect, or the same amount affects me less.

items.title: Withdrawal or rebound
items.text: When I cut down, I have uncomfortable rebound symptoms or feel driven to use again.

items.title: Unsafe use
items.text: Use has happened in dangerous, risky, or unsafe situations.

items.title: Overwhelming event
items.text: I have experienced one or more events that felt terrifying, violating, life-threatening, or deeply overwhelming.

items.title: Unwanted memories
items.text: The event comes back into my mind even when I do not want it to.

items.title: Nightmares
items.text: I have distressing dreams or sleep disruption connected to what happened.

items.title: Reliving or body reactivation
items.text: At times it feels as if I am reliving part of it, or my body reacts as though the danger is happening again.

items.title: Avoidance
items.text: I avoid people, places, conversations, thoughts, or reminders connected to what happened.

items.title: Numb or detached
items.text: I feel emotionally numb, disconnected, or less able to feel close to others than before.

items.title: Negative beliefs or shame
items.text: Since what happened, I have carried strong blame, shame, or negative beliefs about myself, others, or the world.

items.title: On guard
items.text: I stay on guard, watchful, or tense as if danger could return at any time.

items.title: Startle, sleep, or irritability
items.text: I am more jumpy, irritable, or easily startled, and my sleep has often been affected.
